I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for more than fifty years. My husband passed, my children work in the city. I have about 4 mu of contracted land. I don't read, but I know this soil and this weather the way I know my own hands.

I will grow **winter wheat** this winter — I always do. It goes in after the autumn harvest and keeps me through the lean months. Then after I cut the wheat in June, I put in **summer maize** on the same land. This is what my mother did, what everyone here does. The two crops fit together like the seasons themselves. The wheat straw can stay on the ground to keep moisture. My neighbor's son brings his tractor for the big work — planting and harvesting — I pay him in grain.

For seeds, I'll get the improved wheat variety from the township supply co-op — same one as last year, it did well. For maize I'll buy hybrid seed from the village store, the kind everyone uses now. A small packet goes a long way.

For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the wheat is jointing and again when the maize is knee-high. That's what the supply shop tells me to do and what I've seen work. I don't measure precisely — I use the scoops I've always used — but it comes out to roughly what I'll say below.

Irrigation is the hard thing here. Water costs money and the well is shared. For wheat I'll irrigate at sowing if the soil is dry, again before winter, once at jointing. For maize, just once or twice if July is dry, which it usually isn't so much.

I won't overthink it. I've seen bad years and good years. I keep enough grain to eat and sell a little surplus at the village market.
